title: Add Google Antigravity usage collector and panel integration
head: 2a42aa72acbf
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Keyring-only authentication rejects officially supported API-key and keyring-bypass sessions
leads.consequence: A working agy session authenticated via GEMINI_API_KEY or the CLI's file-storage fallback is reported as 'Sign in to see limits'; no remote allowance is attempted. The user may still see local history, but not the actual limits. The exact Secret Service attributes and stored JSON for the ordinary keyring path remain unverified because upstream ships a binary, not that source.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F9; API-key part confirmed by Opus self-check

leads.summary: An empty or expired keyring record is classified as authenticated and Pro
leads.consequence: A nonempty JSON secret such as {} yields auth_ok=True without an access token; expiry is parsed but never consulted. Without local history the code still fabricates two 0% session/weekly limits and a Pro plan, making the bar widget appear because Main.qml treats limits as data. At the next refresh the invented meters persist until authentication is removed or a probe succeeds.

leads.summary: 401 and 403 quota failures are not communicated by the panel
leads.consequence: For 401, probe returns a useful expired-auth helpText but collect_limits leaves usageStatusText empty; the panel renders the help card only when usageStatusText is nonempty. For 403, the HTTP exception is silently ignored and even helpText defaults to the generic 'Run agy' hint. Both fall back to plausible limits and a default Pro plan instead of telling users that authentication or permission needs attention.

leads.summary: Local estimates and last-known allowances render as current account quotas
leads.consequence: When probing fails, an unexpired cached limit or the 50/250-prompt local heuristic is returned without estimated, limitsStale, or any nonempty usageStatusText for transport failures and most HTTP errors. The panel's hero and meters then look identical to live account quotas, even after credentials or the account change. No local data gives invented 0% allowances. On transport failure this record also omits retryAdvised, so Main.qml:83-107 does not attempt its 30-second recovery and waits up to the 900-second refresh unless the panel opens or the user refreshes it. Preserve the source/freshness in the record, label local estimates, and advise a retry on a failed transport.

leads.summary: Stats and quota caches are not keyed to the overridden app root or account
leads.consequence: Switching AGY_DIR within the same HOME reuses a scan from the previous directory for 20 seconds (15 minutes for --limits-only). Changing signed-in accounts while a probe is unavailable reuses the old account's allowance and tier until each cached reset, while treating it as live. The next refresh may continue to display the wrong account's quota. Include resolved root and account identity in cache keys and invalidate on changes.
leads.triage: dropped: low user impact (20 s stats reuse; account switch edge case)

leads.summary: The documented ISO-form history timestamp never enters the local rolling-limit calculation
leads.consequence: collect_local_stats accepts ISO string timestamps, and the new scanner fixture writes precisely one, but calculate_limits compares the raw string to integer millisecond cutoffs. Each comparison raises TypeError and is swallowed, so both rolling windows remain 0% for all ISO-form entries even while 'Today' counts their prompts. Parse timestamps consistently in both readers.

leads.summary: UTC calendar grouping disagrees with the panel's local Today row
leads.consequence: The collector bins day and dates in UTC, whereas Panel.qml computes its Today row from the user's local calendar. For example, at 17:30 in UTC-7 the collector already writes tomorrow's date, so the panel's today row stays empty and yesterday/tomorrow takes the usage. Convert timestamps to local dates before counting or align the consumer.

leads.summary: Quota response edge cases drop groups or display a missing fraction as 0% usage
leads.consequence: If the API returns a non-Gemini group first, it is initially assigned as primary, then overwritten by Gemini without being appended to other_groups. If multiple Gemini groups exist, each earlier one is overwritten. Their quota meters vanish without warning. Missing remainingFraction is also treated as 1.0, i.e. a misleading 0% used, even though the analogous Gemini Code Assist bucket type marks it optional. The producer's real group ordering and omission behavior are not publicly specified, so applicability to real Antigravity accounts is unconfirmed; a sanitized CLI quota payload would settle it.

leads.summary: Removing an existing default-agent file leaves its old selection active
leads.consequence: The new FileView only sets defaultAgentRaw on a successful load. FileView's watcher signals a change on file deletion, reload then signals loadFailed; with no onLoadFailed reset the previous default persists until restarting the shell. Agent.qml already handles that event. Add onLoadFailed to clear the selection; the related #6860 implementation explicitly does so, and a merge with it requires resolving a conflict.

leads.summary: Empty XDG_CACHE_HOME or AGY_DIR resolves to the working directory
leads.consequence: An exported-but-empty XDG_CACHE_HOME makes Path('') relative to cwd, so running the collector in a project writes omarchy/agent-usage/*.json and *.lock into that project instead of ~/.cache, with 0644 stats snapshots. An empty AGY_DIR instead scans cwd/history.jsonl and cwd/brain, potentially reporting unrelated project files as agent usage. Follow the Codex collector's `or` fallback for both paths.

leads.summary: Two other open PRs add the identical Antigravity collector path and id
leads.consequence: Unstacked #8873 and #10400 each add bin/omarchy-agent-usage-antigravity and return id antigravity. Whichever is merged first forces an add/add conflict with this PR and completely different collector semantics; a manual resolution must pick or reconcile one implementation rather than merge duplicate records. Pairwise git merge-file with each PR's merge-base reports markers; GitHub marks each other PR MERGEABLE against its own base, not necessarily against this head.
leads.triage: #8873 corroborates Opus; #10400 verified by coordinator via gh (coordinator/pr-10400.json) and confirmed in Opus self-check

leads.summary: Open #8479 would display Antigravity twice as agy and antigravity
leads.consequence: The other unstacked collector uses a distinct executable name and id `agy` but reads the same ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/history.jsonl. The updater discovers both by filename, writes agy.json and antigravity.json, and Main.qml displays two enabled Antigravity tabs; each tab independently counts the same history. Choose one canonical provider ID and reconcile data before merging either PR. Their README overlap also has a merge conflict, but the double entry survives even if that text is reconciled.

leads.summary: The AI manual's explicit list of supported panel collectors omits Antigravity
leads.consequence: After this PR the manual still states that only Claude Code, Codex, and Fireworks are covered out of the box, despite enabling Antigravity in the widget's manifest. Add Antigravity (or `agy`) at line 37 and keep the README's provider list aligned.

leads.summary: New tests never exercise the quota probe and Panel default-selection behavior
leads.consequence: A plausible mutant that sends the wrong Cloud Code URL or ignores 401/403 still passes: the limits test imports only extract_tier/extract_limits, while the scanner's keyring stub supplies no access token, so probe_antigravity is never called. A mutant that always selects index 0 also passes because the two new Panel assertions are substring checks. Add an isolated urlopen stub that checks request paths and errors and a behavioral provider-index test with a stub default file, including deletion.

leads.summary: Transcript-only usage is silently hidden if history and keyring are absent
leads.consequence: The collector reads transcript modelUsage and todayTotalTokens, but computes totalSessions, activeDays, and totalPrompts only from history.jsonl and conversation_summaries.db. If those files are absent, or only the transcripts remain after a cleanup, and the keyring is absent (including supported API-key or no-D-Bus sessions), it emits positive tokens with ready=false and no limits. Main.qml's providerHasData does not test token totals or modelUsage, so the panel never displays the record at all. Count transcript sessions/dates as a fallback or make the provider-visible predicate consider transcript totals.
leads.triage: dropped: edge case, premise that agy writes transcripts without history unverified

limits: The official google-antigravity/antigravity-cli repository at 8cb7cd1 (1.2.12, 2026-09-27) publishes README, changelog and examples only, not the CLI's keyring writer, transcript writer or quota API client. Thus exact keyring attribute names, JSON shape, transcript format, Cloud Code quota groups and expiry encodings could not be verified at the shipped CLI version. Gemini CLI at 2fe7c2d3f is an analog only: its code_assist/types.ts:250-265 defines a different retrieveUserQuota response with optional remainingFraction, and its setup.ts:177-183 sends metadata where this PR posts {}. Do not infer Antigravity's wire format from Gemini CLI.

Current quattro has additional changes under shell/ and bin/ but its only base-side hunk in the files changed by this PR is Panel.qml's IpcHandler to ShellIpc. A merge using f2b419d9 as base cleanly retains ShellIpc in merges/current-Panel.merge, so that base-side change is not a conflict. The added collector is not yet in current quattro.
No desktop slot or real account was available; no direct keyring or Cloud Code endpoint was queried. Sandbox fixtures use mock secret-tool and mocked urllib.request.urlopen only.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the collector plugs into the agents plugin as intended. `omarchy-agent-usage-update` discovers it by file name, the record id `antigravity` matches the file, the record fields match what `Main.qml` and `Panel.qml` read, the icons resolve by convention, and the new tests, the neighbouring agent tests and `test/cli` pass on the head. With a successful (synthetic) Cloud Code response, tier and Session/Weekly limits come out as the PR describes. The Panel change selects the default agent's tab for `agy`, `claude` and `codex`, and an explicit tab selection still wins.

The main issue is what the panel shows when the live quota call does not succeed: failures are silent, and invented limits and a guessed plan are shown as if they were account data.

### Failed quota calls are silent and show estimated limits as real ones

When the user is signed in, `collect_limits` leaves `usageStatusText` empty for a missing access token, a 401, a network failure and any other HTTP error; among these failures only a 429 that makes the whole probe fail sets it (`bin/omarchy-agent-usage-antigravity:620-657`). The panel shows the status card and replaces the plan line only when `usageStatusText` is non-empty (`shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml:207-213`, `:524-546`), so in these cases the computed "Antigravity authentication expired…" and "Could not reach Antigravity service." texts do not appear.

Instead, when no cached window is still open, the collector emits `calculate_limits`: Session = prompts in the last 5 hours / 50, Weekly = prompts in the last 7 days / 250, weekly reset always `now + 7 days`, under the same labels as the API values (`:528-598`). Nothing in the PR or repository documents where 50 and 250 come from. When the user is signed in and no tier comes from `AGY_TIER`, the config file, the probe, the cache or an enterprise/cloud sign-in, the plan falls back to "Pro" (`:355-379`).

Synthetic runs (stub `secret-tool`, a local HTTP server standing in for Cloud Code; no cache except in the second 401 row):

| Case | `limits` shown | `usageStatusText` | Plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 OK | API values | `""` | from API |
| 401, no cache | estimate (Session 60%, Weekly 12%) | `""` | Pro |
| 401, earlier cache | last cached windows | `""` | cached |
| network failure | estimate | `""` | Pro |
| 429 | estimate | "Antigravity limits rate limited" | Pro |
| signed in, no access token | estimate | `""` | Pro |

Related details:
- The keyring `expiry` is parsed into `expires_at_ms` but never used (`:101-113`); a token that expired two hours earlier was still sent to both endpoints. agy refreshes its token proactively five minutes before expiry (agy CHANGELOG 1.1.23); since that refresh happens in agy itself, a stale keyring token is likely whenever agy has been closed for a while.
- The 429 case pairs the rate-limit status with the help text "Run `agy` to authenticate."
- If `cli.log` changed in the last 5 hours and its tail contains `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` or "rate limit exceeded", Session is pinned to 100% (`:569-582`), which turns the bar icon urgent when Antigravity is the tab shown. What agy writes there, including for the short 429s it retries on its own, was not verified.
- `calculate_limits` compares `timestamp` with integers, so ISO-string timestamps are skipped (`:551-556`): 30 ISO-stamped prompts today gave a 0% estimate. `collect_local_stats` accepts both forms.
- Because the estimate always returns two entries, any signed-in machine without a successful probe gets a non-empty `limits` list, which alone makes the Antigravity tab appear (`Main.qml:219-224`).

**Impact:** after a token expires or the network drops, the panel keeps showing plausible-looking meters and a cached or guessed ("Pro") plan with no hint that they are estimated or stale. The agents README promises that "Auth and endpoint problems replace the plan line and repeat in a card" (`shell/plugins/agents/README.md:12-13`); the Claude collector checks token expiry, reports "Waiting for auth" or "Sign-in expired", says "Claude limits unavailable" when nothing is cached, and sets `retryAdvised` on network failures (`bin/omarchy-agent-usage-claude:809-846`).

**Suggested change:** set `usageStatusText` for each failure (missing or expired token, 401/403, network, other HTTP errors) and give the 429 case its own help text; check `expires_at_ms` before probing; set `retryAdvised` on network failures; leave `tierLabel` empty when the tier is unknown (the hero then reads "Subscription"); and either drop the prompt-count estimate or label it unmistakably as an estimate.

An alternative that avoids reading credentials at all: agy 1.1.11 added `agy -p "/usage" --output-format json`, which the agy changelog describes as answering read-only slash commands "without starting an agent turn, spending quota, or leaving a conversation behind". The same changelog entry notes that unhandled print-mode slash commands "previously fell through as literal prompt text", and third-party stablyai/orca#23426 gates its `/usage` call on agy 1.1.11 or later for that reason, so a version check would be needed. This mirrors how the Codex collector asks `codex app-server`. Its cost per refresh was not measured.

### Scoped Claude/GPT limits disappear if that group comes first

`extract_limits` picks the primary group with `if "gemini" in name or gemini_group is None` (`:201-204`). If "Claude and GPT models" is listed first, it becomes the primary group, is then replaced by the Gemini group, and never reaches `other_groups`.

```text
groups order (synthetic run)    limits returned
Gemini, Claude/GPT              Session, Weekly, Claude/GPT Weekly (20% used)
Claude/GPT, Gemini (reversed)   Session, Weekly            <- Claude/GPT Weekly dropped
```

A bucket without `remainingFraction` is read as 1.0: a Gemini Session or Weekly bucket then shows as 0% used (`:225`, `:234`), and a scoped bucket is hidden (`:250-253`). If the server omits zero-valued fields, as proto3 JSON does by default, an exhausted bucket would look unused; this is a hypothesis, since no real response was captured.

**Impact:** third-party allowance usage can silently vanish from the panel, depending only on response order.

**Suggested change:** select the Gemini group by name first and treat every other group as scoped; treat a missing `remainingFraction` as unknown and skip that bucket.

### Daily stats use UTC dates while the panel uses local dates

`main` uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, and `collect_local_stats` derives today, the 7 recent days and history dates from UTC (`:383-385`, `:415`, `:496`). The panel's Today row and the sync merge use the local date (`Panel.qml:215-222`, `Main.qml:523-531`), as do the Claude and Codex collectors. In a synthetic run at 23:41 UTC with `TZ=Etc/GMT-14`, the local date was 2026-09-28 but `recentDays` ended at 2026-09-27, so the panel would mark no row as Today (inferred from `Panel.qml:674`; the panel was not run).

**Impact:** for users away from UTC, today's prompts and tokens land on the wrong day for part of every day.

**Suggested change:** use local dates (`datetime.now().astimezone()`, converting timestamps to local time) as the other collectors do.

### Token counts can double-count and invent a model row

In `collect_local_stats` (`:462-506`):
- A transcript step without `created_at` counts toward `todayTotalTokens` on every scan but not toward the Today entry in `recentDays`. In a synthetic transcript the two differed (2150 against 1150).
- A step without `usage` is estimated as characters / 4 and added on top. The PR's own fixture shows it: input tokens 122 = 120 `prompt_token_count` + 2 estimated from the user's message, which `prompt_token_count` already includes if it means what it does in the Gemini API.
- A step without `model` (every `USER_INPUT` step in the PR's fixture) is attributed to a hard-coded `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, which can create a phantom model row when another model was used.

It is also unverified whether agy transcripts carry per-step `usage` and `model` at all. Third-party readers estimate tokens from transcript text or read `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<uuid>.db` instead. If the fields are absent, every Antigravity token figure is an unlabelled estimate. A redacted transcript line from agy 1.2.x would settle it.

**Impact:** token totals and per-model rows can be inflated or attributed to a model that was not used.

**Suggested change:** count only model steps that carry `usage` (or read the conversations database if transcripts lack it), skip steps without `created_at` instead of treating them as today, and leave the model unknown rather than defaulting it.

### Unverified quota request shape

Both Cloud Code POSTs send `{}`, discarding the `cloudaicompanionProject` returned by `loadCodeAssist` (`:288`, `:304`). For the sibling `retrieveUserQuota` method, Gemini CLI's `RetrieveUserQuotaRequest` requires `project` (`packages/core/src/code_assist/types.ts:250-253`), and third-party Antigravity quota scripts send `project` to `retrieveUserQuotaSummary` too. This is a hypothesis: no real response was captured. If the server answers `{}` with a differently shaped response, `extract_limits` returns `[]` and, per the first finding, no status is shown; a generic entitlement view in the same shape would show wrong numbers instead.

**Impact:** if the premise holds, Antigravity limits are empty or wrong for real accounts even when the probe succeeds, with no status shown.

**Suggested change:** send the `cloudaicompanionProject` returned by `loadCodeAssist` as `project`, or confirm the request shape first. A redacted capture of agy's own request, or the same account queried with and without `project`, would settle it.

### Smaller notes

- **Sign-in detection:** an `id_token` that fails to decode makes a valid sign-in report "Sign in to see limits" (`:115-126`); the decoded email is never used, so the decode can go or get its own `try`. The lookup also only reads the keyring, while agy supports file-stored credentials when the keyring is bypassed or unreachable (agy CHANGELOG 1.1.26, 1.1.3) and `GEMINI_API_KEY` sessions; those users are reported as signed out.
- **Default-agent watcher:** the `FileView` in `Panel.qml:28-34` has no `onLoadFailed`, so deleting `~/.config/omarchy/defaults/agent` keeps the old default. From Quickshell v0.3.1 source (not run), `FileView` watches only the file and its parent directory, and `~/.config/omarchy/defaults/` is created only when a default is first chosen, so a first-ever default picked while the shell runs would likely not be seen until restart.
- **Documentation:** `manual/17-ai.md:37` still says "Claude Code, Codex, and Fireworks are covered out of the box". The README paragraph at `shell/plugins/agents/README.md:60` was reflowed into a single line of about 770 characters, while the rest of the file wraps near 78 columns, and the `providers` example (`:122-128`) still lists three agents.

**Optional test improvement:** in a mutation run against the three changed or new test files, these mutants all survived: the live probe is never called, the probed tier is ignored, the rate-limit status is never set, the 5-hour estimate never counts a prompt, the panel never selects the default agent, and `agy` no longer maps to `antigravity`. The two assertions the PR adds to the panel test only check that the strings `normalizeAgentId` and `omarchy/defaults/agent` occur, and the scanner test asserts the "Pro" fallback. Its history fixture also uses ISO timestamps and `conversation_id`, while third-party readers of agy's `history.jsonl` see integer milliseconds and `conversationId`. A scanner test against a local fake `CLOUD_CODE_URL` covering 200, 401, 429, network failure and an expired token, a reversed-group case, and a node test that evaluates `providerIndex` (the repository already has `run_node_test`) would catch these.

### Overlapping open PRs

- #8873 and #10400 each add their own `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-antigravity`; #8873 also adds both icon files, and #10400 adds both icons plus `agent-usage-antigravity-scanner-test.sh`. These conflict file-for-file with this PR.
- #8479 adds `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-agy` with record id `agy`. Merged together with this PR, the same tool would get two tabs.
- #6860 implements the same default-agent selection in `Panel.qml`, including `onLoadFailed` handling, and conflicts with this change.

---

## Review information
